en: Sutta Nipāta 5.8 The Young Brahmin Nanda’s Question “There are sages in the world,” [he said].
(Thus spoke the Venerable Nanda:
"People speak thus; they say that this is how it was told to them:
'They call us sages endowed with knowledge.'"
"Or is it truly because of being endowed with life?
"Not by view, nor by hearing, nor by knowledge—
thus do the wise ones here, O Nanda, declare of the Sage."
“Those who wander free from fetters, free from distress, and free from longing— them I call sages.
“Whosoever among these ascetics and brahmins...”
(Thus spoke the Venerable Nanda:
"Some say purification comes through what is seen or heard;
others say purification comes through rules and observances."
They speak of purity in many different ways.
O Blessed One, have those who practice with self-restraint therein crossed over birth and old age, O Fortunate One?
“I ask you, Blessed One, tell me this.
“Whosoever these recluses and brahmins may be,” said the Blessed One, “(‘It is Nanda’).”
They say purification comes through what is seen and heard;
they say purification comes through rules and observances;
they speak of purification in many various ways.
"Even though they live there with self-restraint,
I say they have not transcended birth and old age.
"Whosoever these ascetics and brahmins may be..."
(Thus spoke the Venerable Nanda:
"Some say purification comes through what is seen or heard;
others say purification comes through rules and observances."
They proclaim purity in many ways. If you,
O Sage, say that they have not crossed over the flood,
then who indeed in the world of gods and humans— ?
“O Blessed One, you have crossed over birth and old age;
I ask you, tell me this. “I do not say that all ascetics and brahmins [have done so].”
(The Blessed One rejoices:
"I say that those who are shrouded by birth and old age do not rejoice here in what is seen, heard, or sensed."
Having abandoned all rules and observances,
and having abandoned all manifold forms,
they have fully understood craving and are free from taints.
“Those indeed are the men who have crossed the flood,” so I say.
“I delight in these words of the Great Seer,
well-proclaimed by Gotama as being free from acquisitions.”
Having abandoned whatever has been seen, heard, or sensed,
as well as all rules and observances,
and having abandoned everything of manifold forms—
"Having fully understood craving and being free from taints,
I too declare that I have crossed over the flood.
Thus ends the seventh inquiry, the Question of the Young Man Nanda.
